epics.title: Préparer le host Windows et reprendre les contrats communs

evidence_map.proof: Windows target, CEF/Chromium/cef-rs pins, archive hashes, provenance, protocol version and notices are declared.

evidence_map.entry_point: runtime metadata and Windows native qualification
evidence_map.proof: The signed runtime and same-version development archive were verified on Windows 11 build 26200.0; the manifest declares the Windows 10 1809 floor and bootstrap, sandbox and control-only contracts.

evidence_map.entry_point: explicit fetch and safe extraction CLI
evidence_map.proof: HTTPS provenance, size/SHA-1 when declared/SHA-256 checks, traversal and special-file rejection, bounded extraction and no build.rs or first-use download; fetch security suite passes.
The consumed browser contract commit and protocol version are recorded independently of Linux or another OS qualification.
Absent targets, archive mismatches and unsafe candidates fail closed while an existing runtime is preserved; negative fetch tests pass.
The exported Windows entry point passes sandbox_info, executes subprocess roles before browser initialization, keeps no_sandbox disabled and does not set browser_subprocess_path.
Bootstrap and client roles are separated, x64 PE headers and a real RunWinMain export are required, and unknown client DLLs remain unavailable in contract tests.

evidence_map.entry_point: Windows client build, staging and signature script
evidence_map.proof: The pinned client was built with the same-version CEF development archive, staged with the signed runtime, locally signed for qualification, and executed through the real bootstrap handshake.
Windows runtime discovery is file/manifest based and BrowserRuntime is installed without loading CEF; CEF starts only from a Browser page activation.

evidence_map.entry_point: runtime readiness and staged host verification
evidence_map.proof: Missing or incompatible runtime, bootstrap PE or client export returns unavailable; the supervisor launches the bootstrap executable rather than a DLL and the host requests sandboxing.

evidence_map.entry_point: named-pipe listener and Job Object ownership
evidence_map.proof: The pipe uses owner-scoped SDDL and the bootstrap process is assigned to KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE; no inherited control handle or kill-by-name path is used.
Windows profile tests pass 6/6; production profile creation applies protected SYSTEM, administrators and owner ACLs, and the native receipt reports exactly those entries.
Root locking, ownership, routing, handshake, closure and refused readiness paths are wired; Windows supervisor contract tests pass 4/4 and the native control round trip completed successfully.
Resource release is tied to the owned Job Object and process handles; shutdown has a bounded grace period and no privilege elevation or process-name kill.
Readiness, parent-loss and supervisor failures route to Browser errors while preserving terminal startup and existing profile state.

evidence_map.entry_point: shared BrowserRuntime, authority, ProfileHost and BrowserView
evidence_map.proof: Windows selects target-specific install/supervisor/page adapters while reusing the common controller, dock actions, owners, profiles, descriptors and lifecycle.
The deterministic shared controller path is wired to the Windows ProfileHost and native v3 create/close protocol; no Windows-specific dock rewrite exists.
The target is explicitly development-only, native qualification is not executed, and missing or invalid runtime data leaves public activation unavailable.

evidence_map.entry_point: shared contract metadata and target adapters
evidence_map.proof: The consumed common commit and protocol contract are recorded; the Windows path depends on the shared interfaces, not Linux DONE status or a divergent dock copy.

scope_corrections: Keep EP-001 control-only until EP-002; no native GPU, browser creation or public qualification is claimed.
The review fixed the Windows CEF import-library link emission in build.rs and the common fetch regression caused by an unconditional archive_sha1 lookup.
Runtime packaging remains development-only and must not be treated as Windows sandbox or GPU qualification.

The pinned signed archive and same-version development headers/import library were integrated and qualified through the control-only Windows 11 harness; release signing alignment remains later packaging work.
unapplied_maintenance: Release packaging must align Authenticode signing for chrome_elf.dll, bootstrap and client artifacts.
browser-package.py can make RunWinMain export validation unconditional when release packaging is brought into scope.
epics.validation: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy -p paneflow-app --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --locked -- -D warnings; cargo clippy -p paneflow-browser-host --features cef-runtime --lib --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --locked -- -D warnings; Windows profile tests 6/6; Windows supervisor tests 4/4; browser host tests 2/2; bun test scripts/browser-qualification/fetch.test.mjs 12/12; python -m py_compile; cargo deny check advisories licenses sources; git diff --check; native Windows 11 build 26200 control-only receipt with handshake, sandbox, create and close
epics.progress_note: EP-001 is certified DONE at the control-only tier. The pinned runtime is integrated, the Windows host contracts are tested, and the real CEF bootstrap/control round trip is recorded on Windows 11; GPU, browser-page and release-package qualification remain in later epics.
